intro: The universal ending in the dative: both after the definite article (**dem**, **der**, **den**) and after the indefinite or possessive article (**einem**, **einer**, **meinen**), the adjective in the dative ALWAYS ends in **-en**.

piezas.titulo: Golden rule of the attributive dative
texto: The dative case is the most regular and predictable of all German adjective inflection. Once the preceding determiner marks the dative (**dem**, **der**, **einem**, **einer**, **keinem**, **unserem**), the attributive adjective takes the ending **-en** without exception: **Ich wohne bei dem älteren Nachbarn.** / **Sie hilft der freundlichen Kollegin.** / **Wir sprechen mit den erfahrenen Spezialisten.**
Moreover, in the plural of nouns in the dative, most nouns add a final **-n** if they didn't already end in «-n» or «-s»: **mit den neuen Mietern**, **in den großen Zimmern**.

filas.texto: Er wohnt in dem renovierten Altbau.
Sie fährt mit einem schnellen Zug.

frases.estudio: Hast du gestern dem neuen Nachbarn beim Tragen der Kisten geholfen?
frases.alumno: Did you help the new neighbour carry the boxes yesterday?

frases.estudio: Ja, und danach habe ich der älteren Vermieterin im Erdgeschoss die Dokumente übergeben.
frases.alumno: Yes, and afterwards I handed the documents to the older landlady on the ground floor.

frases.estudio: Die Hausgemeinschaft ist wirklich hilfsbereit. Wir wohnen hier mit sehr freundlichen Leuten zusammen.
frases.alumno: The residents' association is really helpful. We live here with very friendly people.
analisis: the residents' community is very helpful

frases.estudio: Genau, nach dem anstrengenden Umzug fühle ich mich in diesem ruhigen Viertel sehr wohl.
frases.alumno: Exactly, after the exhausting move I feel very much at home in this quiet district.

pregunta.texto: What is the obligatory ending of the adjective in the dative when preceded by a determiner?

opciones.texto: -en
opciones.explicacion: In all genders and numbers, the adjective preceded by an article in the dative ends in «-en».

opciones.texto: -er
opciones.explicacion: The ending «-er» in the dative only appears without article in the feminine, not with a preceding article.

opciones.texto: -em
opciones.explicacion: «-em» is the ending taken by the article or the strong adjective without article, never after «dem».

frase.texto: Der Hausmeister hilft der neu___ Mieterin bei der Reparatur.

opciones.texto: en
opciones.explicacion: After the feminine dative article «der», the adjective always takes the ending «-en».

opciones.texto: er
opciones.explicacion: «neuer» would wrongly duplicate the strong ending of the article «der».

opciones.texto: e
opciones.explicacion: The ending «-e» does not exist in the dative after a determiner under any circumstances.

pregunta.texto: What cooperative action does Jonas's question describe?

frase.texto: Jonas: Hast du gestern dem neuen Nachbarn beim Tragen der Kisten geholfen?

opciones.texto: He asks whether she gave physical help to the newcomer to move his packages from the move.
opciones.explicacion: «beim Tragen der Kisten geholfen» refers expressly to helping the neighbour with his boxes.

opciones.texto: He asks whether the new tenant hired a professional moving company.
opciones.explicacion: It doesn't ask about an external company, but about the personal help given by Sarah.

opciones.texto: He asks whether the neighbour returned the tools borrowed for the renovation intact.
opciones.explicacion: No tools are mentioned, but help carrying the moving boxes.

pregunta.texto: What morphological change does the noun undergo in the plural dative in «den hilfsbereiten Nachbarn»?

opciones.texto: The noun adds a final «-n» characteristic of the plural dative case whenever it is phonetically feasible.
opciones.explicacion: In the plural dative, the article («den»), the adjective («-en») and the noun all add the «-n» mark.

opciones.texto: The noun loses its final consonant to align with the singular feminine gender.
opciones.explicacion: Inflection doesn't remove consonants; it consolidates the nasal «-n» mark.

opciones.texto: The noun remains invariable and the case is marked only by the adverb of manner.
opciones.explicacion: The plural dative case is expressed jointly in the determiner, adjective and noun.

frase.texto: Wir sprechen nach dem anstrengend___ Umzug mit den Eigentümern.

opciones.texto: en
opciones.explicacion: After the preposition «nach», the article «dem» requires the masculine dative with an adjective in «-en».

opciones.texto: em
opciones.explicacion: It is a frequent mistake to confuse the ending of the article «dem» with that of the adjective «-en».

opciones.texto: er
opciones.explicacion: An ending foreign to the singular dative after a masculine definite article.

pregunta.texto: What state of mind and assessment does the tenant express?

frase.texto: Nach dem anstrengenden Umzug fühle ich mich in diesem ruhigen Viertel sehr wohl.

opciones.texto: She expresses deep well-being and calm in her new neighbourhood after completing the laborious move.
opciones.explicacion: «fühlt sich wohl» in a «ruhigen Viertel» after the physical effort of the change of home.

opciones.texto: She laments the constant noise of city traffic near the new flat.
opciones.explicacion: It describes the neighbourhood exactly as quiet («ruhigen Viertel»).

opciones.texto: She demands the immediate cancellation of the contract because of the exhaustion suffered during the transport.
opciones.explicacion: The sentence expresses satisfaction and relief in the new home, not an intention to leave.

pregunta.texto: Which sentence is formulated with absolute syntactic and inflectional correctness in the dative?

opciones.texto: Ich habe mich mit der neuen Kollegin aus dem technischen Bereich unterhalten.
opciones.explicacion: «mit der neuen Kollegin» (feminine dative) and «aus dem technischen Bereich» (masculine dative) apply «-en».

opciones.texto: Ich habe mich mit der neue Kollegin aus dem technischem Bereich unterhalten.
opciones.explicacion: «der neue» omits the obligatory «-n», and «dem technischem» wrongly doubles the «-m».

opciones.texto: Ich habe mich mit die neue Kollegin aus den technischen Bereich unterhalten.
opciones.explicacion: It confuses feminine accusative («mit die») and masculine («aus den») after strict dative prepositions.
